items.title: George Lewis Interview, 1968-10-12
items.q: Donor Adams. The only man that ever played chords and he didn't know the piano. At all.

ctx.x: 된 된 된 된 된 That's right. Joe Peck. Peck. Peck. They call him Joe Peck. He's got a place on our own. He's a big old gal dressed. Joe Peck. And his brother Frank. And after I left there, I didn't... I didn't wait out for him no more, because I'm here. It's a casual. It was a rough idea. I wouldn't make any money. This was all in the 30s? Who was you playing with at the Popeye's? Yeah, it was... Did you get it? Uh... Uh... Uh... Clay Bear, I kept another brother. He was playing drums. Uh... Uh... Uh... Uh... Uh...…

So I went down to a four. Four is kind of hard. It's called a grain of the wood. Now here's a three and a half or three. But these have a more time. I found out this testing regime, you know what I mean? And then I found out that there's a lot of things that I found out. This testing regime, you know what I mean? It don't mean that the readers good. That's the only thing in there. I had to end this year, the slip, of course. But some diamond grain, you know. I was a king. Now for a card, I don't like. No classic…

the music better. You can hear the rhythm and the rhythm is the most important thing in the band. You can hear the rhythm. You got good rhythm. That's what Lawrence was living in. Fred could hear better. Joe. They did put on. You could hear the band and you only got the rhythm there. Joe said I worked him hard. I didn't work him hard. I mean he worked his own self hard. And then if you got the band you got the work man hard. Because most of the leaders don't want to work. They want to put their arm on their lap.…
